quiz.headline: Your team loses hours to copy-paste; a small test could recover some.

ideas.title: Automate the invoice CSV to spreadsheet transfer
ideas.how: You said the team loses most hours copying data between systems, and the sample task is copying a fictional invoice CSV into a second spreadsheet. Test a scripted or spreadsheet-native import (for example, a query or import formula) on the fictional sample only, and compare the time taken against the manual copy.
ideas.hoursBack: Not measured — test recoverable time on a small sample

ideas.title: Add a simple validation check after each transfer
ideas.how: Copying errors are a common side effect of manual transfers. Build a small check on the fictional sample that flags row-count mismatches or totals that don't reconcile between the source CSV and the target sheet, so the team spends less time re-checking by hand.
ideas.hoursBack: Not measured — test recoverable time on a small sample

ideas.title: Free up capacity for customer work with a one-day pilot
ideas.how: You said a recovered day would go to serving customers better. Pick one repetitive transfer, run the fictional-sample test for a week, and log the minutes spent before and after. If the numbers hold, use the logged time to decide whether a wider rollout is worth exploring.
ideas.hoursBack: Not measured — test recoverable time on a small sample

quiz.firstStep: Using only the fictional invoice CSV sample, time one manual copy into the second spreadsheet, then time an import-based attempt on the same file, and record row accuracy for both without touching production data or sending any outbound messages.
quiz.explanation: Rule of thumb: reported hours contribute 50%, company-size band 20%, previous automation experience 30%. It does not establish feasibility, budget or buying intent. Reported task: Copy a fictional invoice CSV into a second spreadsheet. Constraints: Only the fictional sample; no production access or outbound messages.
